todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.
outcome: Finish task 004 by closing the source-less raw-follow generation escape and giving generation-less historical removals and follows durable pre-removal versus post-re-add ordering.
scope: Revise the existing unaccepted task-004 candidate in place. Preserve its public Membership-to-Messaging cleanup collaboration, idempotent cleanup facts, source-aware manual/root/reply ordering, surviving-group behavior, and historic replay support while addressing only the latest two review gaps.

Make raw `Memba.Messaging.follow_conversation/2` conservative after cleanup: a source-less raw follow must not escape a removed-group cutoff merely because an unrelated club membership transition advanced the club-wide generation. Keep caller-provided `authorizing_group_ids` untrusted and continue deriving non-empty source groups only at authoritative current-member or committed message boundaries.

Keep `follow_conversation_as_current_member/2` as the authorized user-facing opt-in path. Ensure it captures both authoritative readable conversation groups and the current membership generation within the stable authorization boundary, so a genuine explicit follow after re-add remains the operation that restores notifications.

Add an integration regression for remove member M from group A at generation G, advance the club generation through an unrelated group-membership transition while M remains absent from A, attempt a source-less raw follow, then re-add M to A. Prove the raw attempt emits no `ConversationFollowed`, creates no projected follow, and does not resume reply delivery; a later authorized current-member follow must still restore normal delivery.

Replace the generation-zero ambiguity for historical facts with a minimal durable, append-only ordering mechanism. First/origin cleanup replay must remove a generation-less `ConversationFollowed` or auto-following root `MessageSent` established before the historical `GroupMemberRemoved`, while retaining equivalent generation-less follow state genuinely established after a historical re-add.

Add focused historical integration and aggregate regressions that exercise actual generation-less event shapes, including both pre-removal cleanup and post-re-add preservation on first cleanup delivery or origin replay. Persist any cleanup decision through Messaging-owned facts and keep the collaboration through public Messaging APIs.

Rerun the focused task-004 suites to preserve initially-unfollowed cleanup, manual/root/reply auto-follow cleanup, surviving-group same-generation causality, genuine generated post-re-add follows, unrelated-follow preservation, cleanup retry/checkpoint ordering, replay/idempotency, accepted task-001 removal behavior, and system-group no-ops.
scope_exclusions: Do not change task identity 004, reset the bounded revision count, or discard any of its six cumulative candidate origins.
Do not restore trust in caller-supplied raw `authorizing_group_ids`, and do not let source-less raw follows inherit an unrelated club generation as proof of renewed authorization.

Do not rewrite historical Membership or Messaging events, mutate foreign-context projections directly, or introduce a broad event-store/projection redesign; use the smallest durable compatibility mechanism that distinguishes the required historical orderings.

Do not weaken the effective-access union: a genuine follow or sender auto-follow authorized through surviving group B remains valid at group A's removal generation, while work sourced only from removed A remains rejected.
Do not change accepted task-001 custom-group removal authorization, transition/idempotency semantics, club roles or membership, last-member behavior, or system-group guards.
Do not implement current query/action authorization, LiveView refresh, or queued provider-handoff work assigned to tasks 009-011.
Do not implement Leave/Remove UI, shared member-row changes, confirmations, post-removal surfaces, or empty-group presentation assigned to tasks 012-014.
Do not edit iteration-064 feature files or implement the remaining browser/domain acceptance and invariant layer assigned to tasks 015-016.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, browser acceptance, or another unscoped full-suite command; task 017 and the deterministic `dev_check` node own the final repository gate.

references.facts: Implementation Plan 2, the acceptance criteria, and Open Technical Decisions require public Messaging APIs, cleanup of every follow source, explicit re-follow after re-add, unrelated-follow preservation, and durable stale-safe ordering.
Iteration 062 established the replay-safe Membership-to-Messaging cleanup collaboration that explicit custom-group removal extends.
Membership owns membership facts, Messaging owns follow state, and collaboration must cross public context APIs rather than foreign aggregate or projection storage.
The Club stream is authoritative for membership lifecycle and must keep historical facts replayable; system-group membership remains a policy-maintained consequence.
Command-side facts carry authority; query projections must not manufacture causal follow authorization.
Historical compatibility must be append-only, replayable, based on immutable source facts, and tested with the actual historical event shape.
Use deterministic process/checkpoint synchronization and avoid timing sleeps in the ordering regressions.

`follow_conversation_command/1` strips source groups but currently stamps every raw follow with `Membership.current_group_membership_generation/1`; `follow_conversation_as_current_member/2`, root send, reply, and `establish_message_sender_follow/1` are the authoritative source-capture paths.
`membership_generation/1` maps generation-less `GroupMemberRemoved` events to zero and forwards event identity/checkpoint metadata through the public cleanup API during origin replay.
`event_membership_generation/2` reconstructs monotonic aggregate state for generation-less historical group membership events, while new facts carry explicit generations.

`normalize_generation/1`, `follow_allowed?/4`, and `apply_unfollow/2` currently compare generation-less follows and historical cleanup at zero, so equal-generation cleanup deletes a genuinely later legacy follow.
Member-scoped cleanup cutoffs protect delayed sender auto-follows for conversations created after cleanup and must stay consistent with the selected compatibility ordering.

The existing raw-forged-source and production surviving-group root tests cover the prior review; extend focused integration coverage for an unrelated generation advance and actual generation-less pre-removal/post-re-add histories.
Current replay tests normalize legacy facts but the post-re-add preservation example uses generated generations 1 and 2 rather than truly generation-less historical facts.

The current revise verdict identifies exactly two uncovered branches: source-less raw follow escape after an unrelated generation advance, and ambiguous ordering among generation-less historical removal/re-add/follow facts.

constraints: Keep this as revision attempt seven for the same pending obligation and build on the current candidate rather than replacing its accepted behavior.
A source-less raw follow after any applicable cleanup cutoff must remain unable to create effective follow state regardless of later unrelated changes to the club-wide membership generation.

An authorized current-member follow after a genuine re-add must derive current source groups and current generation at the stable authorization checkpoint and must restore ordinary future notification eligibility.
Non-empty source attribution must come from authoritative current read/write membership or from a committed message event whose source was captured at that authoritative boundary.

The historical compatibility mechanism must distinguish immutable pre-removal from genuinely post-re-add generation-less follow facts durably on first delivery and replay; do not rely on transient timing or projection state alone.

Cover both manual `ConversationFollowed` and sender auto-follow `MessageSent` historical shapes unless direct inspection proves they share one fully exercised ordering path and the returned evidence explains that equivalence.

Preserve cleanup checkpoint synchronization, per-group cutoffs, conversation-wide historic cutoffs, ordinary-unfollow history, completed cleanup IDs, public add/remove return modes, and system-group behavior.
Keep edits limited to the raw/current-member stamping boundary, historical cleanup ordering collaboration, directly affected command/event compatibility, focused tests, and necessary code comments.
completion_evidence_required: List changed paths and identify how raw source-less follows are prevented from inheriting unrelated club-generation authority while authorized current-member, root, and reply paths retain trusted source and generation capture.

Identify the regression proving remove A, unrelated membership-generation advance, source-less raw follow while absent, and re-add A produce no `ConversationFollowed`, projected follow, or reply delivery until a new authorized current-member follow.

Describe the durable compatibility fact or ordering evidence used for generation-less history and why it remains correct on first cleanup delivery, retry, handler restart, and replay without rewriting old events.
Identify regressions proving both removal of a generation-less pre-removal manual/auto follow and preservation of generation-less follow state genuinely established after a historical re-add.

Confirm prior initially-unfollowed cleanup, manual/root/reply cleanup, surviving-group manual/root/reply causality, genuine generated post-re-add follow, unrelated follow, cleanup retry/checkpoint interleaving, replay/idempotency, and Everyone/Admin regressions remain passing.
Report exact exit statuses and test counts for both focused test commands, plus `git diff --check`, on the handoff state.

Confirm accepted task-001 behavior remains unchanged: explicit custom-group removal reuses the Membership removal fact, exact retry emits no new Membership fact, and club roles/membership plus system-group guards are preserved.
